final.investment_thesis:
The debate converges more than it divides, and the burden falls on deciding whether 3.05% is the right total exposure rather than on adding or liquidating. All three risk seats — aggressive, conservative and neutral — proposed the identical total target of 3.05% with keep_shares, and neither the Research Manager nor the Trader dissented. That unanimity is not laziness; it reflects a genuine split between the destination and the entry, and the sizing should honor both.

The bull wins the destination. The business evidence was never rebutted and the bear conceded 'nothing supports a bearish business stance': 9M FY2026 revenue +16.15%, FQ3 +16.36%, FQ3 gross margin 50.06% (+357bps), FQ3 EPS +28.7%, 9M FCF $110.2B (+52.4%), $62.2B net cash, and 48.7% incremental FQ3 operating margin. The primary trend is likewise confirmed rather than decayed: price 316.83 is 12.7% above a 200-SMA at 281.10 that has risen 40 consecutive sessions, the 10-EMA/50-SMA/VWMA/mid-band stack was reclaimed in three sessions, and ATR has compressed 22% to 7.667.

The bear wins the entry, and that is what caps size. AAPL closed inside the unfilled 07-31 gap (310.69–329.59) only ~2% above its floor and ~5.9% below its top, with trapped supply overhead at 319.28 and 321.62–323.45 — a repair zone, not a breakout. The bear's reward/risk arithmetic is correct and was never answered: waiting for a close above 319.28 raises entry to at least 319.28 while the first objective remains 329.59, so the payoff to a ~309 stop is roughly 1:1, not the 1.6:1 claimed; the bull cannot simultaneously claim today's price and demand breakout confirmation. Confirmation is genuinely absent: MACD -1.719 versus a -0.984 signal (below zero, below signal), RSI 53.85, MFI 50.37, 08-19 volume only 0.95x the 20-day average, a flat 50-SMA at 309.44, and VWMA down 21 straight sessions to 307.76 below the 50-SMA. The evidence gaps also stand — no segment revenue, geographic mix, forward guidance, valuation multiples, consensus estimates or insider data, plus a five-day news hole from Aug 12–16 with a large share of records unobserved — so the Services-led margin inference cannot be verified from this fact set.

Sizing: why 3.05% is the right total exposure. A concrete higher allocation of 6–8% is favored by the intact primary uptrend and the 16% growth/50% margin/$110B FCF franchise, but it is not justified today because it requires paying up into overhead supply on unconfirmed volume with MACD below zero; the trigger is narrative only — a daily close above 329.59 (gap top) on volume above 65M with MACD back above its zero line. A concrete lower allocation of 0–1%, or outright liquidation to 0, is favored by the flat 50-SMA, the 21-session VWMA decline, the EU take-rate precedent (26% IAP, 20% alternative payments, 15% link-outs, 5% Core Technology Commission — a modest, already-traded negative that also reduces DMA tail risk), inventory +94% and the missing segment/guidance/valuation data; but it is not justified because the business case is conceded by both sides, the 200-SMA is rising, and selling a 3% stake to sit in 0%-yield cash would pay fees (already $26.93 cumulative) to forfeit participation for zero fundamental gain. The 3.05% retained is therefore the midpoint of a genuine evidence conflict, not an anchored discount applied to yesterday's holding.

Cash opportunity cost versus downside, in account terms. About 96.9% of equity ($96,905) earns no interest. If AAPL merely fills the gap to 329.59 (+4.0%), the current 3.05% contributes roughly 0.12% of total equity, versus about 0.24% at a 6% target; a push to the 333–340 July shelf (+5% to +7%) widens that to roughly +0.18% versus +0.35%. Downside is comparably bounded: a failure at 319–323 that breaks the 307.8–309.4 pivot and retests 302.25/300 costs the position about 0.35% of total equity, and even a slide to the 200-SMA at 281.10 (~11% below) costs roughly 0.34%. Neither outcome dominates the account, which is precisely why neither risk avoidance nor cash opportunity cost should override the other here, and why a repeated proportional trim with no fresh total-target justification would be the wrong action.

Economic purpose of the retained 3.05%. It is not an unspecified 'observation position' — observing the tape requires no shares. It is the smallest allocation that produces real, fee-free account P&L if the gap fills or a product-cycle catalyst lands, while keeping the defined narrative risk (307.8–309.4 pivot, then 302.25/300) at roughly a third of one percent of equity. Fees for a round trip on ~$3,049 would consume a meaningful share of that expected move, so the marginal transaction is not worth executing in either direction today.

Prior lessons are the reason this is Hold and not Underweight. The 2026-08-10, 08-11 and 08-12 AAPL Underweights all bled five-day alpha (+1.7%, +4.8% and -0.9% raw respectively, with the first two clearly against the call) by reducing on momentum decay inside a stacked rising structure, and the 08-12 reflection codified the fix: size the rating by distance-to-invalidation, and when the falsification level sits only ~3% above entry, the honest call is Hold with a plan to sell into strength rather than a proportional cut. That applies directly here: the invalidation (307.8) is only ~2.8% below spot. What would change the call: a daily close above 329.59 on >65M volume with MACD back above zero justifies raising toward 5–6% (and toward 6–8% if the 333–340 shelf is reclaimed); a close below 307.8 justifies cutting toward 1–2%, and a close below 302.25/300 justifies exiting to 0. A sub-48% gross-margin print with inventory above ~$13B or a soft FQ4 guide at the late-October print converts this to a genuine Sell. Stated gaps: no valuation multiples, no consensus estimates, no segment or geographic mix, no options or implied-vol data (so any hedge cannot be priced from this evidence), and an incomplete news sample through Aug 12–16.
